onboarding.title: Welcome to TapLayer
onboarding.body:
Trigger key = one key, many actions

After you assign a trigger key, single-tap / double-tap / long-press can each trigger a different action. The trigger key is intercepted by TapLayer (to tell the tap patterns apart), so pick a key you rarely use.

Pro tip: zero-conflict setup (recommended)

Use a programmable mouse/keyboard driver (e.g. Logitech G HUB, Razer Synapse) to remap a physical button (like the DPI button) to F13-F24 (keys that don't exist on keyboards), then use F24 as the trigger key. Example: F24 single-tap = Ctrl+C (copy), double-tap = Ctrl+V (paste), long-press = screenshot. Since F24 has no physical key, intercepting it has zero side effects.

Basic setup

Use low-usage keys like ScrollLock, Pause, Insert as trigger keys.

Mouse buttons

Use your mouse side buttons (X1/X2) or middle button as trigger keys — zero conflict. When recording a mouse button, move the cursor over the key display area first, then click.

Warning: Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Win are NOT suitable as trigger keys — they will be intercepted and combinations like Ctrl+C/V will stop working. Also avoid the mouse left/right buttons (all clicks get intercepted; you will be warned on confirm).

Emergency: Press Alt+Ctrl+F9 anytime to pause/resume TapLayer and restore your keyboard and mouse.

help.title: Usage Guide
help.intro: TapLayer translates how you press the trigger key (single, double, triple, long press) into the output keys you bind. The trigger key is recorded by you (a mouse side button, F24, or a chord like A+S).
help.section.bind: Use gesture output keys in other software
help.bind.keynote: Key point: do NOT try to "record a hotkey" with your mouse/trigger key. When any software is recording, it captures the physical key pressed at that instant (e.g. F24) — not the output key TapLayer translates it into.
help.bind.how1: 1. In TapLayer, set the output of a gesture (e.g. long press) to the key you want (e.g. F5).
help.bind.how2: 2. In the target app (e.g. a screenshot tool), set its hotkey to F5 directly — press F5 on your keyboard in its recorder dialog.
help.bind.how3: 3. Now, when you long-press the trigger, TapLayer outputs F5 and the target app responds.
help.bind.note: Why recording does not work: the recorder captures the physical key (F24). This is a system-level behavior; TapLayer cannot block other apps from seeing the physical key.
help.bind.alt: If the output key is special (e.g. F13-F24) and your keyboard has no such key: some apps let you type the key code manually; otherwise this scenario cannot be set up via "recording".
help.settings.trigger: Trigger key: use the "Record Hotkey" button on the trigger card at the top of the binding editor to change it — it does not have to be F24, chords are supported.
help.settings.pause: Pause / exit: the app lives in the system tray. Closing the window asks whether to quit or minimize to tray; right-click the tray icon also exits. While paused, all gestures are disabled.
